finding.claim: Embed extension fetches any attacker-supplied https:// URL server-side by default because the domain allowlist is only installed when embed.allowed_domains is non-empty, and its default is []. No host, IP-range, count, or redirect restriction exists anywhere in the path.
finding.source: Attacker-authored Markdown: a line consisting solely of an https:// URL (EmbedStartParser.php:34 prefix check, :39 parseLinkDestination, :47 end-of-line check).
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP request via Embed\Embed::getMulti in OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43, executed during DocumentParsed (EmbedExtension.php:45, priority 1010).

trace.note: Accepts any line starting with https://; attacker chooses host.
Creates Embed block carrying the attacker URL.
allowed_domains defaults to [].
Reads allowed_domains.
If empty, DomainFilteringAdapter is NOT wrapped, so no host check runs.
EmbedProcessor registered with the raw (unfiltered) adapter.
All top-level embeds passed to adapter->updateEmbeds in one batch; no cap on count.

finding.guards_checked: https-only prefix (EmbedStartParser:34) limits scheme only. DomainFilteringAdapter (DomainFilteringAdapter.php:47-61) exists but is bypassed when allowed_domains is empty. No private/loopback/link-local IP block, no redirect validation, no per-document fetch limit in this repo. Fallback setting (EmbedExtension.php:29) only affects output, not whether the fetch happens. Confidence: high for the repo-level fail-open; actual SSRF reach depends on the consumer's network and on the embed/embed library's redirect behavior, which is not vendored here.

finding.claim: Embed HTML fetched from a remote page is emitted raw, bypassing html_input (escape/strip). If an attacker can control the oEmbed/extracted HTML, this yields stored XSS in the rendered page. The allowlist suffix match makes this reachable through attacker-hosted subdomains of allow-listed shared hosts.
finding.source: Remote page content at an attacker-chosen URL. Reachable when allowed_domains includes a shared suffix (e.g. a hosting domain) that the attacker can publish under, or when no allowlist is set (see embed-ssrf-fail-open-default).
finding.sink: Raw output of $node->getEmbedCode() in EmbedRenderer::render, with no HtmlFilter applied.

trace.note: Suffix match: any host ending in '.'+allowed domain passes, so attacker.<allowed-shared-host> is admitted.
Reads extractor->code; non-null when the remote page yields embeddable HTML.
setEmbedCode stores the remote html verbatim.
Non-null embed code is kept (not replaced by fallback).
SINK: returns getEmbedCode() raw; html_input is never consulted.

finding.guards_checked: html_input is applied to HtmlBlock/HtmlInline (HtmlBlockRenderer.php:46, HtmlInlineRenderer.php:46) but not to Embed nodes. No sanitizer in EmbedRenderer or the adapter. Allowlist host check (DomainFilteringAdapter.php:51-55) is the only control; it checks only the submitted URL, not redirects or oEmbed discovery targets. Confidence: PLAUSIBLE. Whether the external library returns attacker-controlled html for a generic page is not verifiable from this repo.

finding.claim: allow_unsafe_links defaults to true, so Markdown links with javascript: (and other unsafe) schemes render as live href attributes unless the consumer explicitly opts out.
finding.sink: href attribute emitted in LinkRenderer.php:49 and clicked by a user in the consumer's page.

trace.note: Default allow_unsafe_links = true.
forbidUnsafeLinks = !true = false.
Unsafe-protocol check (RegexHelper::isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe) short-circuited by forbidUnsafeLinks=false.
SINK: attrs['href'] = raw destination.
Xml::escape prevents attribute breakout only; it does not neutralize the javascript: scheme.

finding.guards_checked: RegexHelper::isLinkPotentiallyUnsafe (RegexHelper.php:251-258) is a correct scheme check with whitespace/control-byte normalization, but it runs only when allow_unsafe_links is false. Attribute filter (AttributesHelper::filterAttributes) also gated on the same flag. Exploitable in any deployment that renders untrusted Markdown without explicitly setting allow_unsafe_links=false. Documented library default; flagged because it is unsafe for untrusted input.
